issues.title: Reduce the per-call cost of the bit-backend threshold read
issues.notes: Closed at c596d6a6 after 3 rework rounds plus one owner-granted counter reset. cargo-ci and code-review both pass. Mechanism: the bit-backend threshold is published into an AtomicUsize beside an AtomicBool resolved flag; each publication site stores the threshold Relaxed then the flag Release, and active_simd_min_words loads the flag Acquire before loading the threshold Relaxed. One-shot resolution preserved (a selection resolves active(), so a later install returns AlreadyResolved) and install publishes only after ACTIVE.set succeeds. Round history: R1 missed REQ-03's test entirely and silently regressed one-shot resolution by removing the only active() call from the selection path; R2 fixed both but published through two relaxed stores with no happens-before, which code-review caught as a real race; R3 followed the lead's own WRONG instruction to use a usize::MAX sentinel, which broke v1 schema semantics because design §2.1 documents usize::MAX as a meaningful simd_min_words; R4 (after owner reset) restored try_new and closed the race with Release/Acquire. The lead then corrected the amendment's inaccurate 'at most once per process' claim about the cold path directly.

DEC-B6: karatsuba_min_degree is not sweepable from a bench target. A bench links gf2-core as an external crate, so it can name only pub items, and both arms are private (mul_schoolbook_impl at crates/gf2-core/src/field/poly.rs:2484, mul_karatsuba_raw at :2531); the only public entry is the threshold-driven dispatcher FieldPoly::mul, and poly.rs:72 documents the omission deliberately. Resolution per design §5 condition 5: the emitted profile OMITS the field so it inherits the default at load — emitting it carrying 32 would be a @/inv/benchmark-backed-performance defect, since a profile must not claim an unmeasured value. Verified the loader supports omission: JsonPolynomial fields are Option<Option<usize>> (tuning/mod.rs:903-907) and from_json falls back to CONSERVATIVE. TuningProfile::to_json cannot express omission, so the harness constructs the emitted document with only the four swept fields and validates it through from_json, which is what §2.7's output discipline asks. Rejected: adding pub forcing entry points (public API against the poly.rs:72 decision, outside this issue) and reordering 5ecc9bf8 behind 697fc55b (rejected for scope, not ordering — 5ecc9bf8 is not upstream of 50b47eae, so that sequencing would not have inverted the DAG). Tracked forward as 389aa4de.

The post-cutover comparison FAILS: bit_backend/popcount/words=1 at ratio 1.182311 and words=8 at 1.064214, both above tau_cell=5%; tau_set holds at 0.998853. The control arm sits at 0.972476 and 1.002702 at those cells, so the reading predeclared in across-build-control-arm-v1.md §4.3 attributes the excursion to the cutover. Resolution: remove the cost, do NOT widen the tolerance and do NOT amend REQ-04. Filed c42720ce inside the epic; 50b47eae depends on it and re-runs the unmodified procedure afterwards. LEAD CORRECTION TO THE CHOSEN MECHANISM: the option text said 'compiled-in floor below which the profile is not consulted'. That cannot fix the words=8 cell — a floor removes the read only below itself, so fixing words=8 needs a floor above 8, while SIMD_MIN_WORDS_DEFAULT is 8 and 5ecc9bf8's committed calibration selects 4 for this field; any such floor would put the boundary beyond the profile's reach and make the calibration inert. c42720ce therefore requires the read to be made cheap while the profile keeps governing every pinned size. The owner's intent (make REQ-04 pass without touching the tolerance) is preserved; only the mechanism differs, and the correction was reported.
